NOT claimed then: cli/src/lsp.ts, tools.ts (heavily contended: re-check), diagnostics.ts, doctor.ts, core/tool_groups.ts, core/capability_definitions/lsp.ts, cli/test/lsp_*.

## ADDENDUM 2026-11-22: the owner's scope supersedes the "Decisions" defaults above
The owner pasted a four-area scope (full text in memory file lsp-scope-owner-2026-11-22.md). Changes to this plan:
- IN SCOPE NOW: rename of symbols, files and folders; code transformations (extract function, move function between files); type and call hierarchy; signature and documentation lookup; incremental diagnostics immediately after the agent's edits; clangd and jdtls beside pyright, rust-analyzer, gopls (and typescript-language-server); capability discovery; cold-start and memory management; prompt guidance (prefer LSP for semantic queries, grep/read for text, comments, literals).
- Units: LS-1 hardening and document synchronisation (this plan's LS-1); LS-2 position encoding and roots; LS-3 navigation: references, document and workspace symbols, type definition, implementation, call hierarchy, type hierarchy, signature help; LS-4 incremental diagnostics after edits (advisory to the turn; never the completion verdict); LS-5 semantic refactoring: rename (prepareRename + rename), file and folder rename (workspace/willRenameFiles), code actions resolved to edits (extract, move); LS-6 lifecycle across five servers: capability discovery drives which tools are offered, restart with backoff, warm-up, memory and idle shutdown, clangd and jdtls with pinned weekly cases, `nexus doctor` findings, tool descriptions and system-prompt guidance.
- Design constraints for LS-5 (one gate, plan principle 2): a language server NEVER writes files. Every WorkspaceEdit, whether returned by rename or a code action or sent by the server in `workspace/applyEdit`, is converted into proposed edits that Nexus applies through its normal edit path: approval mode, verification-file guard, path protection, diff shown to the operator, recorded in the receipt, followed by verification. The client answers `workspace/applyEdit` with applied:false-until-approved semantics (decide exactly: either refuse and re-request via the edit path, or stage). `workspace/executeCommand` only for an allowlist of commands known to return or request edits, per server; anything else refused. Resource operations in a WorkspaceEdit (create, rename, delete file) go through the same gate and are refused outside the workspace. A rename that touches a verification file is subject to the guard like any other edit.
# Real language servers (CS-6)

`cli/src/lsp.ts` (the `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` tools) is tested in the ordinary suite against `cli/test/fixtures/fake_lsp_server.mjs`. `cli/test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts` also runs the product's own `LspBridgeManager` against real servers on fixture projects written to a temporary directory. Navigation cases use a three-source-file import/re-export chain (or equivalent package-level call chain) and require hover and definition to resolve through that project. The `lsp-real-servers` workflow runs it weekly (Monday 04:17 UTC) and on demand. It is not a required check.

Per server the test asserts that a file with one deliberate error yields `status: "ok"` with an error diagnostic whose message names it; a clean file yields `status: "ok"` with an empty list (a published report, which is not `unavailable`); and a manager whose server cannot start yields `unavailable`. The extended lifecycle test also verifies trust and read-only refusal before launch, diagnostics and incremental fixes in a 64-source-file fixture, and that a killed server does not leave stale clean diagnostics visible. It then starts a fresh manager and confirms the changed workspace can be diagnosed again.

| Server | Command the product starts | Fixture error | Needed to run |
|---|---|---|---|
| typescript | `typescript-language-server --stdio` | `const n: number = "..."` under `strict` | `typescript`, `typescript-language-server` |
| python | `pyright-langserver --stdio` | `x: int = "..."` | `pyright` |
| rust | `rust-analyzer` | `let x: i32 = "..."` in a Cargo project | `rust-analyzer` |
| go | `gopls` | `var x int = "..."` in a module | `gopls` |

## Skip versus fail

The server is looked up on the PATH the product gives a language server (`buildLspEnvironment`: absolute entries only, none inside the workspace), and where the server has a `--version` mode it is run under that same environment. A server that is absent, or present but not runnable there, SKIPS with the reason. `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE` turns that into a failure: `1` (or `all`) requires every server, a comma list (`typescript,python`) requires those. Ids: `typescript`, `python`, `rust`, `go`. The workflow sets `typescript,python`; rust-analyzer and gopls are best-effort installs there, so their cases run when the install worked and skip otherwise.

```sh
npm i -g typescript typescript-language-server pyright   # or put their bin directory on PATH
cd cli && node scripts/run_tests.mjs test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts
NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE=1 node scripts/run_tests.mjs test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts   # missing server = failure
```

The suite runs under a throwaway HOME, so a tool installed only for the current user (`pip install --user`, `~/.cargo/bin` reached through the real HOME) is invisible. The workflow installs with `npm -g`, and sets `RUSTUP_HOME` and `CARGO_HOME` for the rustup proxy. The real-server workflow pins Node 22.22.1, Go 1.27.4, Rust 1.95.0 with its rust-analyzer component, gopls v0.24.0, TypeScript 5.6.3, typescript-language-server 4.3.4, and pyright 1.1.390. All four servers are required; an installation or startup failure fails the run.

## What it found

The first real run showed the default launch commands for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python were missing `--stdio`; both servers print a usage error and exit without it, so `lsp_diagnostics` for those files was always `unavailable` in practice. Fixed in `getServerForFile`; a test that needs no server pins the arguments.

## What it does not cover

- The trust and sandbox gates with a real server (they are tested with the fake server; a gated manager never starts one).
- A larger real project: navigation uses three source files, but there is no large workspace-wide diagnostics fixture, incremental-edit sequence, or server crash/restart scenario.
- Server versions other than the pinned ones (typescript 5.6.3, typescript-language-server 4.3.4, pyright 1.1.390; gopls (`@latest`: v0.16.2 stopped building on a newer runner Go on 2026-11-18) and the runner's rust-analyzer are unpinned).
- Hosted-runner result (manual run 44323291710 on `3732d911`, 2026-11-18): **typescript-language-server, pyright and gopls passed** (a deliberate error reported, a clean file a real empty report, a broken server `unavailable`), which also confirms on real servers that the default launch needs `--stdio`. **rust-analyzer failed**: the product reported "not installed or failed to start" although the rustup proxy answered `--version` in the test's probe. The cause is not diagnosed (it needs a host with the rust-analyzer component to reproduce); the Rust case therefore runs as a `todo` (reported, not failing the job) unless `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE` names it, and the workflow requires `typescript,python,go`. A manual run of that change on its branch (run 44323915622) completed successfully: 5 pass, 0 fail, 1 todo (Rust).
- **rust-analyzer (2026-11-18, reproduced locally in an isolated rustup home):** two separate problems, both fixed. (1) *Setup:* the workflow added the component to the toolchain pinned by the repository's `rust-toolchain.toml`, but the product launches the server in a fixture directory outside the repository, where rustup uses the **default** toolchain, which had no rust-analyzer ("failed to start" in about 150 ms); the test's `--version` probe ran from the repository and could not see it. The probe now runs in the fixture directory and the workflow adds the component from a directory with no override. (2) *Product behaviour:* `lsp_diagnostics` used to return on the first `publishDiagnostics`, which rust-analyzer sends **empty** before it has loaded the Cargo project and analysed types, so a file with a type error was reported clean. A server can now be marked `awaitProgress` (rust-analyzer is, in the built-in table): the client advertises `window.workDoneProgress`, answers the server's own requests (`window/workDoneProgress/create`, `workspace/configuration`, ...), tracks `$/progress`, and after the first publish waits until the server's progress has ended and been quiet for 1.5 s (or, if it reports none, a 4 s grace), always within the caller's timeout. Server-free tests (`lsp_progress.test.ts`) pin it with a fake staged server (four mutations each fail a test); the real-server case passes locally against rust-analyzer 1.100.0 (about 13 s for a first call on a tiny crate).
- **Hosted validation of this change:** manual run 44334778543 on the branch (2026-11-18): typescript-language-server, pyright, gopls and rust-analyzer all pass (6 tests, 0 fail, 0 todo; Rust about 18 s). Earlier runs of the same workflow found the setup mismatch (44323291710), the empty-first-publish behaviour (44332636397) and a `gopls@v0.16.2` build break on the runner's newer Go (now `@latest`).
- **Three-file navigation extension:** hosted run [44606102675](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44606102675) on commit `99c6049f` (2026-11-19) passed all 10 tests with `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE=typescript,python,go,rust`: all four real servers passed the diagnostics and navigation cases, with 0 failures, skips, or todos. This is a small three-source-file chain, not evidence for large-project behavior.
- **Hover and definition (CS-6 follow-up):** each real server is asked, through the product, to hover and go to the definition through a three-source-file project (positions are 1-based, as `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` take them); the call is retried until the case timeout because servers answer only after analysis, and the definition must point into the defining file. This checks a small import/re-export chain; it does not establish behavior on large projects.
- The lifecycle case runs against all four pinned real servers. Its generated project has 64 source files; it is a bounded scale check, not a performance benchmark or evidence for arbitrarily large repositories. Crash recovery is checked by starting a fresh `LspBridgeManager`; automatic restart within an already-running manager is not asserted.
- **Cost and limit:** a first Rust diagnostics call on a large crate can take as long as the project load, and is bounded by the caller's timeout, after which the existing "published no diagnostics" `unavailable` applies. Later calls return as soon as progress is quiet. A change to an already-open file is not waited on separately: the latest published list is returned.
- Rust diagnostics after an already-open file changes send the negotiated `textDocument/didSave` notification and wait for an 8-second minimum settling window (still bounded by the caller's timeout), because the real-server test reproduced a version-matched but stale `rustc` diagnostic immediately after an edit. This improves convergence but adds latency to Rust checks after edits; it does not establish a server-independent guarantee that every diagnostic is current.

## Pinned hosted environment (2026-11-20)

The workflow pins the Go toolchain and gopls to Go 1.27.4 and gopls v0.24.0, matching hosted run [44606741719](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44606741719). It installs Rust 1.95.0 with the rust-analyzer component and makes that the default toolchain because the product starts rustup's proxy from fixture directories outside the repository. The workflow makes TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust mandatory, so setup drift cannot silently turn a missing server into a skipped test. The pinned workflow passed all four real-server cases in hosted run [44670790609](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44670790609) on commit `f87ff07f` (2026-11-20).

# LSP maturity and enhancement: scope proposal and plan (read-only pass, 2026-11-22, code at release/v1.3.0 b1a4b4f6; `lsp.ts` = cli/src/lsp.ts, 663 lines; verify every line number by reading)
Owner request (verbatim): "add maturity and enhancement of lsp to the priority list." Priority 6, after PF-1, PF-2, GV-4, GV-3, VR-1.

## What exists
- Client cli/src/lsp.ts, no dependency. Server by file extension only (getServerForFile ~530-549): .rs rust-analyzer (awaitProgress), .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx typescript-language-server --stdio, .py pyright-langserver --stdio, .go gopls. Unmapped: .mts .cts .mjs .cjs .pyi. An override table (opts.servers ~506-509) is never passed by the product (cli/src/tools.ts ~1009-1018).
- spawn(cmd, args, {cwd: rootPath, env}) ~125-129, no shell; stderr DISCARDED (~130). buildLspEnvironment ~33-55 (MCP allowlist + toolchain vars; PATH keeps only absolute entries not resolving into the workspace). Stricter than commands' environment.
- NEVER sandboxed: the gate refuses to start a server when read-only, untrusted, or any sandbox is set or required (cli/src/tools.ts ~1010-1016); a refusal also stops running servers.
- Framing: Content-Length, 16 MiB cap, oversized stream -> SIGKILL. initialize ~151-165 (5 s): no general.positionEncodings, no workspaceFolders, no initializationOptions, no clientInfo. Server capabilities ignored except textDocumentSync.save.
- syncFile ~354-394: didOpen once, then full-text didChange + didSave when disk differs; ONLY the queried file is synced; NO didClose anywhere.
- firstDiagnostics ~419-436 returns any cached list at once, else waits for the first publish; with awaitProgress polls until progress idle, quiet 1.5 s (or 4 s grace) and 8 s since an edit (~397-417).
- Timeouts: manager default 5000 ms (~587), used unchanged by the tool (cli/src/tools.ts ~1641); requests 8000 ms (~280).
- Server-initiated requests answered ~230-235, 318-324: workspace/configuration -> one null per item; everything else -> result null.
- Shutdown ~478-488: `shutdown`, then `exit` and SIGTERM in the same tick; no wait, no SIGKILL escalation, no process group.
- One manager per RustCoreBridge, one client per command+args, reused; concurrent starts de-duplicated.
- Tools: lsp_hover, lsp_definition (path, line, character; "1-indexed", unit unstated), lsp_diagnostics (path): cli/src/core/capability_definitions/lsp.ts:3-108; mutating false, effect "exec" (review mode asks per call); in READ_ONLY_TOOLS (parallel batch); tool group `lsp` hidden until the operator text matches /\b(lsp|language server|go to definition|hover|diagnostics)\b/i or the model calls enable_tools (cli/src/core/tool_groups.ts ~25-29).
- Diagnostics output: sanitised, redacted, 1-based, capped 50 records / 32,000 chars, fenced as untrusted (cli/src/diagnostics.ts ~219-237, 256-269). Hover: raw server text, NOT fenced or capped (cli/src/tools.ts ~1610-1622). Definition: raw JSON, file:// URIs with 0-based ranges (~1624-1636).
- TUI: a verb mapping only. `nexus doctor`: nothing. Configuration: none. Telemetry: none. Manual: three one-line entries (docs/USER_MANUAL.md ~620-622).
- Tests: cli/test/lsp_honesty.test.ts (13, fake), lsp_progress.test.ts (4), lsp_trust.test.ts (13), cg3_diagnostics_evidence.test.ts, lsp_real_servers.test.ts (real; weekly workflow .github/workflows/lsp-real-servers.yml, not a required check; pins Node 22.22.1, Go 1.27.4, TypeScript 5.6.3, typescript-language-server 4.3.4, pyright 1.1.390, Rust 1.95.0 + rust-analyzer, gopls v0.24.0). Existing fake: cli/test/fixtures/fake_lsp_server.mjs.

## Defects established by reading (numbers are referenced by the slices)
Correctness: (1) STALE BUFFERS in other open files: once file B was opened by any LSP call the server keeps B's old text after the agent edits B on disk; answers for A that depend on B are computed against old B and reported `ok`. (2) A diagnostics list cached before the file's first open is returned as current. (3) The tool's 5 s timeout defeats the Rust settling loop (8 s post-edit window): the first Rust lsp_diagnostics is expected to return "published no diagnostics within 5000ms" (docs record 13-18 s for a first Rust call). (4) Position units undefined: no positionEncodings negotiation, no conversion; a column counted in code points or bytes is wrong on any line with non-ASCII text before the symbol. (5) Definition output is 0-based file:// URIs while inputs and diagnostics are 1-based workspace paths. (6) URI built from the unresolved path; a server that canonicalises publishes under a different URI and the waiter never fires. (7) Hints reported as "information". (8) workspace/applyEdit gets null instead of {applied: false}; unknown methods get success instead of MethodNotFound. (9) Hover and definition have no readiness wait: a first call commonly returns "No hover info" / empty with success false, indistinguishable from "no symbol here".
Robustness: (10) a missing binary: the `error` handler does not reject the pending initialize, so it appears to cost the full 5 s on every call; failures are not cached; "not installed" and "failed to start" are conflated; stderr is discarded. (11) Shutdown: no wait, no SIGKILL; a server ignoring SIGTERM or its children can survive; the shutdown request's 8 s timer is not unref'd. (12) Unbounded state: `opened` holds the full text of every file ever touched; diagnosticsMap grows; no file-size cap. (13) No cancellation ($/cancelRequest, AbortSignal). (14) progressSeen is shared and reset by any edit although LSP calls run in parallel. (15) One root, no workspaceFolders (monorepos).
Security: (16) code execution by a server is INSIDE the existing trust decision (untrusted, read-only and sandboxed sessions are refused before spawn; tested); in a trusted workspace a server runs project code unsandboxed with the user's HOME, with no prompt in auto mode. (17) NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE=1 trusts any workspace. (18) Hover text is an UNFENCED injection surface (doc comments from the workspace). (19) A sandbox means no LSP at all: if a default sandbox lands, LSP becomes unavailable by default.
Usability: (20) no configuration, no doctor finding, no manual section. (21) docs/LSP_REAL_SERVERS.md contradicts itself.

## Maturity checklist today
Lifecycle: partly. Protocol conformance for the subset used: partly. Fresh answers (never stale as ok): NOT MET. Bounded resources: partly. Deterministic timeouts and clear failures: partly. Environment parity: met (stricter). Sandbox parity: not met (refuse-only). Position encoding: NOT MET. Server-request handling: partly. Multi-root: not met. Output bounded and fenced: partly. Pinned real-server CI: met for 4 languages, weekly, not required. Configuration, doctor, telemetry: not met. Docs: partly.

## Proposed units
| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LS-1 | Hardening: re-sync or close every open document before each query; clear the cache on first open; key by canonical path; per-server timeouts with readiness retry; fast, distinct "not installed" vs "failed to start" with a stderr tail; awaited shutdown with SIGKILL escalation; bounded open-document set and file-size cap; fenced, capped hover; workspace-relative 1-based definition output; hint severity; correct applyEdit and unknown-method replies | each defect (1-3, 5-12, 18) has a fake-server test that fails before and passes after; no surviving process; the weekly job green with product-default timeouts | M | P1 |
| LS-2 | Position encoding and roots: negotiate positionEncodings; convert between a documented model-facing unit and the negotiated one; send workspaceFolders; nearest project root (reuse the roots discoverTypechecks finds) | non-ASCII fixtures (BMP and astral) resolve the right symbol on fake and real servers; a nested-project fixture gets diagnostics per sub-project | M | P1 |
| LS-3 | First enhancements behind an experimental setting: warm-up, lsp_references, document and workspace symbols, symbol-anchored positions (line + symbol text; the client computes the column); `nexus doctor` findings per server (found, version, why refused); user-level config; spans; manual section; docs corrected | schemas generated from types; outputs fenced and capped; doctor test; one real-server case per new operation | M | P1 |
| LS-4 | More languages (clangd first), advisory post-edit diagnostics, pull diagnostics | pinned weekly case per language; advisory output never changes a verdict (tested) | M | P2 |
Gates: G-3 add cases (an untrusted, read-only or sandboxed session starts no server; project config cannot name a server command; no LSP result raises a verdict). New G-LS: the weekly real-server run green on the release head, triggered manually before tagging.

## Decisions (recommended defaults; awaiting the owner)
D-LS1 in v1.3.0: LS-1, LS-2, LS-3; LS-4 stretch. D-LS2 no server for an untrusted workspace. D-LS3 keep refusing under a sandbox in v1.3.0 and say so in doctor and the tool error (running a server inside bwrap is a v1.4 candidate; REVISIT if a default sandbox ships). D-LS4 rename and code actions OUT of v1.3.0 (if ever: only a proposed text edit through the normal edit gate; never executeCommand). D-LS5 current four languages + clangd (P2). D-LS6 server configuration at user level only. D-LS7 keep effect "exec". D-LS8 LSP is advisory; the type-check gate stays authoritative; LSP never satisfies or blocks the gate. D-LS9 no auto-download of servers.

## Reference (XERJ, opencode corpus, index flagged not verified complete; client code not retrieved)
opencode: LSP off by default with a warning that servers get out of sync and CLI type-checks are often better; lazy start, reuse; per-server config {disabled, command[], extensions[], env, initialization}; ONE experimental `lsp` tool with read-only operations (goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, goToImplementation, call hierarchy); no rename, code action or formatting; auto-download of servers. TOOK as ideas: the config shape, the read-only operation set as the boundary, an experimental flag, "LSP advisory, CLI type-check authoritative". REJECTED: auto-download; project-level config naming a command without a trust decision; a single multiplexed tool. Nothing copied.

## LS-1 slices (S2-S5 share cli/src/lsp.ts: merge one at a time)
S1 CHARACTERISATION TESTS, no product change, NEW FILES ONLY: cli/test/fixtures/fake_lsp_scripted.mjs (a scripted fake server; leave the existing fake alone) + cli/test/lsp_characterization.test.ts. Pin, each as CURRENT behaviour with a `todo` twin stating the target: stale second-file buffer; list cached before first open; symlinked workspace URI mismatch; elapsed time and message for a missing binary; initialize timeout; a server that ignores SIGTERM; the applyEdit and unknown-request replies; hint severity; definition output shape; hover with fence markers; non-ASCII column pass-through; the 5 s vs 8 s interaction (staged fake); growth of the open-document map. Run on Node 22 and 24 if available (process handling).
S2 freshness (defects 1, 2, 6): cli/src/lsp.ts. S3 timeouts and readiness (3, 9, 10): lsp.ts + cli/src/tools.ts (one line ~1641 + messages). S4 lifecycle and bounds (8, 11, 12, 7): lsp.ts. S5 output (5, 18): tools.ts, diagnostics.ts, capability_definitions/lsp.ts. S6 docs and CI: docs/LSP_REAL_SERVERS.md, lsp_real_servers.test.ts, the workflow; the manual section waits for the USER_MANUAL.md claim.
Claimed by others when planned: cli/src/core/agent_support.ts, execution_tracking.ts, core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_view.rs, docs/USER_MANUAL.md, cli/test/harness.test.ts, sandbox.ts, types.ts, index.ts, agent.ts. ## ADDENDUM 2026-11-22: the owner's scope supersedes the "Decisions" defaults above

- Units: LS-1 hardening and document synchronisation (this plan's LS-1); LS-2 position encoding and roots; LS-3 navigation: references, document and workspace symbols, type definition, implementation, call hierarchy, type hierarchy, signature help; LS-4 incremental diagnostics after edits (advisory to the turn; never the completion verdict); LS-5 semantic refactoring: rename (prepareRename + rename), file and folder rename (workspace/willRenameFiles), code actions resolved to edits (extract, move); LS-6 lifecycle across five servers: capability discovery drives which tools are offered, restart with backoff, warm-up, memory and idle shutdown, clangd and jdtls with pinned weekly cases, `nexus doctor` findings, tool descriptions and system-prompt guidance.
- Design constraints for LS-5 (one gate, plan principle 2): a language server NEVER writes files. Every WorkspaceEdit, whether returned by rename or a code action or sent by the server in `workspace/applyEdit`, is converted into proposed edits that Nexus applies through its normal edit path: approval mode, verification-file guard, path protection, diff shown to the operator, recorded in the receipt, followed by verification. The client answers `workspace/applyEdit` with applied:false-until-approved semantics (decide exactly: either refuse and re-request via the edit path, or stage). `workspace/executeCommand` only for an allowlist of commands known to return or request edits, per server; anything else refused. Resource operations in a WorkspaceEdit (create, rename, delete file) go through the same gate and are refused outside the workspace. A rename that touches a verification file is subject to the guard like any other edit.
# Real language servers (CS-6)

`cli/src/lsp.ts` (the `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` tools) is tested in the ordinary suite against `cli/test/fixtures/fake_lsp_server.mjs`. `cli/test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts` also runs the product's own `LspBridgeManager` against real servers on fixture projects written to a temporary directory. Navigation cases use a three-source-file import/re-export chain (or equivalent package-level call chain) and require hover and definition to resolve through that project. The `lsp-real-servers` workflow runs it weekly (Monday 04:17 UTC) and on demand. It is not a required check.

Per server the test asserts that a file with one deliberate error yields `status: "ok"` with an error diagnostic whose message names it; a clean file yields `status: "ok"` with an empty list (a published report, which is not `unavailable`); and a manager whose server cannot start yields `unavailable`. The extended lifecycle test also verifies trust and read-only refusal before launch, diagnostics and incremental fixes in a 64-source-file fixture, and that a killed server does not leave stale clean diagnostics visible. It then starts a fresh manager and confirms the changed workspace can be diagnosed again.

| Server | Command the product starts | Fixture error | Needed to run |
|---|---|---|---|
| typescript | `typescript-language-server --stdio` | `const n: number = "..."` under `strict` | `typescript`, `typescript-language-server` |
| python | `pyright-langserver --stdio` | `x: int = "..."` | `pyright` |
| rust | `rust-analyzer` | `let x: i32 = "..."` in a Cargo project | `rust-analyzer` |
| go | `gopls` | `var x int = "..."` in a module | `gopls` |

## Skip versus fail

The server is looked up on the PATH the product gives a language server (`buildLspEnvironment`: absolute entries only, none inside the workspace), and where the server has a `--version` mode it is run under that same environment. A server that is absent, or present but not runnable there, SKIPS with the reason. `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE` turns that into a failure: `1` (or `all`) requires every server, a comma list (`typescript,python`) requires those. Ids: `typescript`, `python`, `rust`, `go`. The workflow sets `typescript,python`; rust-analyzer and gopls are best-effort installs there, so their cases run when the install worked and skip otherwise.

```sh
npm i -g typescript typescript-language-server pyright   # or put their bin directory on PATH
cd cli && node scripts/run_tests.mjs test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts
NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE=1 node scripts/run_tests.mjs test/lsp_real_servers.test.ts   # missing server = failure
```

The suite runs under a throwaway HOME, so a tool installed only for the current user (`pip install --user`, `~/.cargo/bin` reached through the real HOME) is invisible. The workflow installs with `npm -g`, and sets `RUSTUP_HOME` and `CARGO_HOME` for the rustup proxy. The real-server workflow pins Node 22.22.1, Go 1.27.4, Rust 1.95.0 with its rust-analyzer component, gopls v0.24.0, TypeScript 5.6.3, typescript-language-server 4.3.4, and pyright 1.1.390. All four servers are required; an installation or startup failure fails the run.

## What it found

The first real run showed the default launch commands for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python were missing `--stdio`; both servers print a usage error and exit without it, so `lsp_diagnostics` for those files was always `unavailable` in practice. Fixed in `getServerForFile`; a test that needs no server pins the arguments.

## What it does not cover

- The trust and sandbox gates with a real server (they are tested with the fake server; a gated manager never starts one).
- A larger real project: navigation uses three source files, but there is no large workspace-wide diagnostics fixture, incremental-edit sequence, or server crash/restart scenario.
- Server versions other than the pinned ones (typescript 5.6.3, typescript-language-server 4.3.4, pyright 1.1.390; gopls (`@latest`: v0.16.2 stopped building on a newer runner Go on 2026-11-18) and the runner's rust-analyzer are unpinned).
- Hosted-runner result (manual run 44323291710 on `3732d911`, 2026-11-18): **typescript-language-server, pyright and gopls passed** (a deliberate error reported, a clean file a real empty report, a broken server `unavailable`), which also confirms on real servers that the default launch needs `--stdio`. **rust-analyzer failed**: the product reported "not installed or failed to start" although the rustup proxy answered `--version` in the test's probe. The cause is not diagnosed (it needs a host with the rust-analyzer component to reproduce); the Rust case therefore runs as a `todo` (reported, not failing the job) unless `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE` names it, and the workflow requires `typescript,python,go`. A manual run of that change on its branch (run 44323915622) completed successfully: 5 pass, 0 fail, 1 todo (Rust).
- **rust-analyzer (2026-11-18, reproduced locally in an isolated rustup home):** two separate problems, both fixed. (1) *Setup:* the workflow added the component to the toolchain pinned by the repository's `rust-toolchain.toml`, but the product launches the server in a fixture directory outside the repository, where rustup uses the **default** toolchain, which had no rust-analyzer ("failed to start" in about 150 ms); the test's `--version` probe ran from the repository and could not see it. The probe now runs in the fixture directory and the workflow adds the component from a directory with no override. (2) *Product behaviour:* `lsp_diagnostics` used to return on the first `publishDiagnostics`, which rust-analyzer sends **empty** before it has loaded the Cargo project and analysed types, so a file with a type error was reported clean. A server can now be marked `awaitProgress` (rust-analyzer is, in the built-in table): the client advertises `window.workDoneProgress`, answers the server's own requests (`window/workDoneProgress/create`, `workspace/configuration`, ...), tracks `$/progress`, and after the first publish waits until the server's progress has ended and been quiet for 1.5 s (or, if it reports none, a 4 s grace), always within the caller's timeout. Server-free tests (`lsp_progress.test.ts`) pin it with a fake staged server (four mutations each fail a test); the real-server case passes locally against rust-analyzer 1.100.0 (about 13 s for a first call on a tiny crate).
- **Hosted validation of this change:** manual run 44334778543 on the branch (2026-11-18): typescript-language-server, pyright, gopls and rust-analyzer all pass (6 tests, 0 fail, 0 todo; Rust about 18 s). Earlier runs of the same workflow found the setup mismatch (44323291710), the empty-first-publish behaviour (44332636397) and a `gopls@v0.16.2` build break on the runner's newer Go (now `@latest`).
- **Three-file navigation extension:** hosted run [44606102675](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44606102675) on commit `99c6049f` (2026-11-19) passed all 10 tests with `NEXUS_LSP_REQUIRE=typescript,python,go,rust`: all four real servers passed the diagnostics and navigation cases, with 0 failures, skips, or todos. This is a small three-source-file chain, not evidence for large-project behavior.
- **Hover and definition (CS-6 follow-up):** each real server is asked, through the product, to hover and go to the definition through a three-source-file project (positions are 1-based, as `lsp_hover` and `lsp_definition` take them); the call is retried until the case timeout because servers answer only after analysis, and the definition must point into the defining file. This checks a small import/re-export chain; it does not establish behavior on large projects.
- The lifecycle case runs against all four pinned real servers. Its generated project has 64 source files; it is a bounded scale check, not a performance benchmark or evidence for arbitrarily large repositories. Crash recovery is checked by starting a fresh `LspBridgeManager`; automatic restart within an already-running manager is not asserted.
- **Cost and limit:** a first Rust diagnostics call on a large crate can take as long as the project load, and is bounded by the caller's timeout, after which the existing "published no diagnostics" `unavailable` applies. Later calls return as soon as progress is quiet. A change to an already-open file is not waited on separately: the latest published list is returned.
- Rust diagnostics after an already-open file changes send the negotiated `textDocument/didSave` notification and wait for an 8-second minimum settling window (still bounded by the caller's timeout), because the real-server test reproduced a version-matched but stale `rustc` diagnostic immediately after an edit. This improves convergence but adds latency to Rust checks after edits; it does not establish a server-independent guarantee that every diagnostic is current.

## Pinned hosted environment (2026-11-20)

The workflow pins the Go toolchain and gopls to Go 1.27.4 and gopls v0.24.0, matching hosted run [44606741719](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44606741719). It installs Rust 1.95.0 with the rust-analyzer component and makes that the default toolchain because the product starts rustup's proxy from fixture directories outside the repository. The workflow makes TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust mandatory, so setup drift cannot silently turn a missing server into a skipped test. The pinned workflow passed all four real-server cases in hosted run [44670790609](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions/runs/44670790609) on commit `f87ff07f` (2026-11-20).

content.text:
Slice S3 is implemented and uncommitted in `/home/mike/nexus-wt/ls1c`; nothing was blocked by a file outside the allowed set. Everything below was run on Node 24 only, with no real language server on this host, so the Rust post-edit rule in particular is unproven against rust-analyzer. The worktree was clean at restart and the files you named were identical to what I had read.

## Files changed
- `cli/src/lsp.ts`
- `cli/src/tools.ts` (the three LSP handlers only, 20 lines; manager construction and the gate are untouched)
- `cli/test/lsp_readiness.test.ts` (new, 22 tests)
- `cli/test/lsp_characterization.test.ts`, `cli/test/lsp_freshness.test.ts`, `cli/test/lsp_progress.test.ts`
- `cli/test/helpers/lsp_scripted.ts` (options `timings`, `gate`, `args`; `scenarioFile`, `turnSignal`, exported `FAKE`)
- `cli/test/fixtures/fake_lsp_scripted.mjs` (`loadedOn`; `"never"` for hover and definition)

## State machine
Exposed as `LspClient.status()` and `LspBridgeManager.serverStatus(file)`, returning `{server, state, forMs, detail?, cause?, crashes?}`. No doctor finding or sidecar event was added.

| State | Meaning | `lsp_diagnostics` | `lsp_hover` / `lsp_definition` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `not_started` | Never started, or the gate refuses | Starts it; a refusal returns the gate's reason | Same |
| `starting` / `initializing` | Spawned / `initialize` sent | Waits for the start | Same |
| `indexing` | Progress in flight or ended less than the quiet period ago; or no progress reported, nothing answered yet and still inside the warm-up period. An `awaitProgress` server stays here until a progress cycle ends | Staged server: unavailable, "is still analysing after N (detail); what it has published for F so far is not final. Ask again shortly." Other servers: pull reply or push evidence as in S2 | A non-empty answer is returned. An empty one is asked again until the deadline, then unavailable: "is still indexing after N (detail) and has no hover information for F:L:C yet; this does not mean there is none." |
| `ready` | Progress ended and quiet; or it has answered; or the warm-up is over | Answer, or the S2 "published no diagnostics" message | Answer, or success with the plain "nothing here" statement |
| `failed` | Cause is one of `not_installed`, `spawn_failed`, `exited`, `initialize_timeout`, `crashed`, `crash_loop` | Unavailable with the cause message, plus fenced stderr when there is any | Same message as the error |
| `stopped` | `shutdown()` / `shutdownAll()` | The next query starts it again | Same |

A cancelled call returns "The diagnostics query for F was cancelled." or "LSP request '…' was cancelled".

## Timeouts
All are in `LSP_TIMINGS`, overridable per server (`LspServerSpec.timings`) and by the manager option `timings`.

| Constant | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `LSP_START_TIMEOUT_MS` | 10 s | All four servers answered inside the old 5 s limit on hosted runs 44606102675 and 44670790609; doubled. A judgement. |
| `LSP_WARM_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | 5 s | The value the tool always passed. Also the timeout of one hover or definition request (was 8 s). |
| `LSP_COLD_START_ALLOWANCE_MS` | 5 s | Equal to the warm timeout: no first-query time is recorded for typescript-language-server, pyright or gopls, so nothing longer is justified. |
| `RUST_ANALYZER_COLD_START_ALLOWANCE_MS` | 25 s | First Rust call measured at about 13 s locally and 18 s hosted; 40% headroom. |
| `LSP_PROGRESS_QUIET_MS` | 1.5 s | Unchanged. |
| `LSP_EDIT_SETTLE_MS` | 8 s | Unchanged number; now only the fallback when no progress cycle follows an edit. |
| `LSP_READINESS_RETRY_MS` | 250 ms, doubling to 2 s | A judgement. |
| `LSP_START_FAILURE_RECHECK_MS` | 30 s | A judgement. |
| `LSP_RESTART_BACKOFF_MS` / `LSP_MAX_RESTARTS` | 1 s doubling / 3 | A judgement. |

**Cold-start decision: a bounded longer first wait.** With 13 to 18 s measured, a 5 s return would end three or four calls in a row as "still indexing", each a model round trip, where one waiting call returns the real answer. That is how I read "manage cold-start indexing times".
- The allowance counts from the server's start, not from the call, so a second call never starts it over.
- A call made after the allowance is spent waits only the warm timeout and reports the same state with a larger elapsed time.
- `warmUp(file)` starts indexing ahead of the first query.

The tool handler passes no timeout; the manager's timings decide. An explicit `timeoutMs` to `mgr.diagnostics` is still honoured exactly.

## "Nothing here" and the agent loop
`cli/src/core/run_turn.ts` (lines 945 and 1028) sends `receipt.output` when `success` is true, otherwise `Error executing <tool>: ${receipt.error || "Unknown error"}`. The old `{success: false, error: undefined}` therefore became "Unknown error". The handlers now return `success: true` with the statement as output:
- "No hover information at a.ts:1:1: the language server answered and has nothing for this position."
- "No definition found for a.ts:1:1: the language server answered and has nothing to go to from this position."

Shapes of real answers are unchanged.

## Start-failure messages, verbatim
- `Language server not installed: gopls was not found on PATH. Install it with: go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest` (for a command given as a path: `… was not found.`)
- `Language server '<cmd>' failed to start: exit code 3.`
- `Language server '<cmd>' failed to start: it could not be executed (ENOENT).`
- `Language server '<cmd>' did not answer initialize within 10 s; it was killed.` (SIGKILL)
- `Language server '<cmd>' crashed (killed by SIGKILL); it is restarted by the next query after 1 s.`
- `Language server '<cmd>' crashed 4 times (last: killed by SIGKILL); not restarting until PATH changes or Nexus is restarted.`

The command is looked up on the filtered PATH before spawning, and the spawn `error` event rejects the pending start. Start failures are remembered for 30 s or until `process.env.PATH` changes.

## Stderr
- **Bounded:** a 4096-byte ring; the report quotes the last 400 characters.
- **Sanitised:** `redactPlain` runs on the whole ring before the cut, then `sanitizeDiagnosticMessage` from `diagnostics.ts` strips control characters and escapes, defuses fence markers and makes it one line.
- **Fenced:** kept in `LspFailure.stderrTail` and shown only through `fenceUntrusted("language server stderr, last output", …)`, on the lines after the trusted sentence. `diagnostics.ts` was imported, not edited.

## `CURRENT` tests removed
Each failed against the fix before removal (saved output: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/43bcbb67-2cff-4fa8-a05e-f8aa598df73b/scratchpad/s3/current_tests_fail_evidence.out`). All are replaced by `FIXED` tests and their todo twins are gone.

| Removed test | Duration of the failing run |
|---|---|
| Defect 10, missing binary | 20 ms |
| Defect 10, exit with stderr | 82 ms |
| Defect 10, initialize never answers | 10026 ms |
| Defect 3, false clean | 5091 ms |
| Defect 3, post-edit | 3361 ms |
| Defect 9 | 88 ms |
| Defect 14 | 5111 ms |

## Other tests that changed
- **`CURRENT (defect 22)`:** one assertion. A single `LocationLink` is still read as empty, so it now yields the new success statement instead of `{success: false, "[]"}`. That statement is wrong for this case; the defect stays pinned for S5.
